passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Marie Curie (1867–1934) was a physicist and chemist.
• In 1903 she became the first woman to win a Nobel Prize.
• She won a second Nobel Prize, in chemistry, in 1911.
• She remains the only person to have won Nobel Prizes in two different sciences.
stem: The student wants to emphasize an achievement of Curie's that no one else has matched. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Marie Curie remains the only person to have won Nobel Prizes in two different sciences.
Marie Curie, who lived from 1867 to 1934, worked as both a physicist and a chemist.
In 1903, Marie Curie became the first woman ever to be awarded a Nobel Prize.
In 1911, Marie Curie was awarded her second Nobel Prize, which was in chemistry.
steps: The goal: an achievement no one else has matched.
"The only person" to win in two different sciences is unmatched by anyone.
Being the first woman is a first, but others have since won; the remaining choices describe her life without that unique feature.
key: Look for wording in the notes that matches the goal: here "only."
